beats.text: You and your partner go to bed at different times. That costs more than sleep!
A study compared a hundred fifty couples: morning people, night owls, and mixed pairs.
The mismatched couples had more conflict. Less serious talk. Less time together. And one more thing.
A newer study tracked couples with sleep sensors. When wives were happier with the marriage, the couple slept more in sync.
You don't have to be the same type. One idea: go to bed together. The night owl can get up again.

sources: Larson, Crane & Smith (1991), Morning and night couples: The effect of wake and sleep patterns on marital adjustment, Journal of Marital and Family Therapy 17(1), 53–65 – 150 couples; mismatched wake/sleep patterns went with less marital adjustment, more conflict, less time in serious conversation and shared activities, and less frequent sex.

Gunn, Buysse, Hasler, Begley & Troxel (2015), Sleep concordance in couples is associated with relationship characteristics, Sleep 38(6), 933–939 – couples wore wrist actigraphs for 10 days; minute-by-minute sleep-wake concordance 53–88%; high marital satisfaction in wives went with higher concordance; correlational.
